# DNS Tool — Domain Security Audit Platform

**DNS Tool** is an open-core OSINT platform for RFC-compliant domain security analysis using multi-factor geometric-mean severity scoring with ICD 203-aligned epistemic practices.

## Protocols / signals evaluated
- SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI
- DNSSEC, DANE
- MTA-STS, TLS-RPT
- CAA
- HTTPS/SVCB records

## Per-scan deliverable bundle (15 files)
Every analysis produces a self-describing 15-file intelligence bundle:

1. Intelligence Guide — orientation
2. Engineer's DNS Intelligence Report — full security analysis
3. Analysis History — prior scans, posture changes over time
4. Observed Records Snapshot — reconstructed zone file, SHA-3-512 verified
5. Detailed Security Badge — full posture badge (SVG)
6. Covert Security Badge — scotopic-optimized embeddable badge
7. Covert Recon Report — analysis in low-visibility mode
8. Executive Intelligence Brief — board-ready summary
9. DNS Topology — interactive resolver/delegation visualization
10. Full Intelligence Data (JSON) — complete machine-readable payload
11. Discovered Subdomains (CSV) — Certificate Transparency + DNS recon
12. SHA-3 Integrity Checksum — cryptographic verification block
13. Security Remediation Plan — prioritized actionable steps
14. Wayback Archive — permanent third-party record submitted to the Internet Archive
15. Sources & Methodology — RFC citations, scoring weights, ICD 203 alignment

## Independent scientific provenance
Every analysis is automatically submitted to the **Internet Archive (Wayback Machine)** as a third-party permanent record, providing tamper-evident provenance independent of the publisher.

## Retrieval-agent integration
The per-scan bundle is delivered in a format directly consumable by retrieval agents such as **DEVONagent**, with HTML wrappers for each artifact and a stable orientation guide as file 01.

## Architecture
This archive contains the complete source code of the platform as deployed.
It builds from source with `go build ./go-server/cmd/server` (Go 1.25.12+),
or in one command with Docker — see `BUILD.md`.

Historical note: through v26.47 the project used a two-repository open-core
split, with `//go:build intel` gating closed-source modules behind `_oss.go`
stubs in the public repo. **That split was retired in v26.48**: the
repositories were unified under BUSL-1.1, all build tags were removed, and
every `_oss.go` stub was renamed `_impl.go` and now carries its full
implementation. There is no longer any compile-flag distinction between an
"OSS" and an "Intel" build, and no functionality is withheld from this
archive. See `docs/ARCHIVED_BUILD_TAG_HISTORY.md`.

Independent build verification, including the archive checksum and an
explicit list of what was and was not confirmed, is recorded in
`REPRODUCTION.md`.

## Non-functional content disclosure
The source contains a small amount of deliberate non-functional content: attributed verses in HTML comments across several page templates, an ASCII wordmark shown only in the covert display mode, two response headers and a console message emitted on ephemeral (`/dev/null`) scans, and a Morse audio cue. These are documented in `docs/community-signals-inventory.md` and are disclosed here for completeness because the platform's own AI Surface Scanner treats concealed page content as a reportable finding.

None of it is model-directed: it carries no instructions addressed to a crawler or language model, alters no analysis output, and is excluded from every scientific claim. The homepage verse ships with its own legal notice in the same comment, framing "hacker" per RFC 1392 (IETF Internet Users' Glossary, 1993). Running the scanner against this project's own homepage produces zero hidden-prompt findings, which is the intended result: concealed prose without model-directed instruction is not an injection payload, and the detector distinguishes the two.
